hypothesis: Two historical peers that track the leading candidate and its most complementary challenger can identify useful specialist switches more precisely than a single peer. Each candidate embedding records its abilities in their four joint success states.
onboarding: Use exactly the same 200 common prompt IDs per seed as the original balanced panel. Choose two peers from the 75 historical models using those 200 candidate grades. Fit 20 task-by-state abilities with a historical donor prior and 75 donor weights. Candidate grades from other prompts and seeds are excluded.
query: Predict the four historical states jointly from the incoming prompt and independently generated helper answers. Fit within-state historical residual readouts. A text-only control trains the same model using only question text. The main version uses eight existing helpers. An auxiliary live-peer version, if available, additionally reads the gated UNA response. No candidate runs on evaluation questions.
confirmation: Use the intersection of the new 2,556-question release reserve and the five original audited tasks, excluding every canonical group touched by any of the three 200-question probe panels. Exclude the entire new reserve and all probe groups from every supervised query-side fit. Refit upstream TextMF with all 112 known IDs after excluding every group in the new reserve, then restrict its scores to the same candidate roster. Earlier 4,985 results were known at design time. Treat replays there as secondary. Retain each method and the deployed seed 11 regardless of scores.
selection: Fix the primary 95-dimensional readout, compare its text-only control, and show a 20-dimensional state-mean ablation. Select no method or coefficient on the new reserve. Report accuracy, maximum routing share, paired intervals, fixed-candidate controls and seed-specific deployment.
